summary: This Dockerfile snippet sets up a PHP-FPM container and optionally installs PHP-CS-Fixer (a code formatting tool). It defines configuration arguments at the top, pulls a PHP base image, then conditionally downloads and installs the php-cs-fixer.phar executable if the install flag is enabled.

explanations.2: ARG creates a build-time variable that can be overridden when building the image; this sets the PHP version to 8.2 by default.
explanations.7: This ARG defaults to 'true', meaning PHP-CS-Fixer will be installed by default unless you explicitly pass --build-arg PHPCSFIXER_INSTALL=false when building.
explanations.9: This ARG sets which version of PHP-CS-Fixer to download; it's separated from the install flag so you can independently control whether to install it and which version to use.
explanations.14: The FROM directive uses the PHP_VERSION variable from line 2 to select which base image to build on—in this case, PHP 8.2 with FPM (FastCGI Process Manager).
explanations.19: These ARG lines re-declare the variables inside the new build stage; they need to be re-declared because each stage starts fresh, and we need access to these values for the RUN command that follows.
explanations.24: The 'set -e -x' makes the shell exit immediately if any command fails and print each command before running it, helping catch and debug errors during the build.
explanations.26: This if-statement checks whether PHPCSFIXER_INSTALL equals 'true'; only if it does will the following commands inside the conditional block execute.
explanations.28: Printf with ANSI escape codes prints a colored message to the build log (magenta background) to make the installation step visible during the build process.
explanations.30: Curl downloads the php-cs-fixer.phar file from GitHub's releases page, using the version variable to construct the exact download URL, and saves it to /usr/local/bin/.
explanations.32: Chmod +x makes the downloaded .phar file executable so it can be run as a command from the shell.
